q: What is the EcoVadis carbon scorecard, and what do its levels mean?
title: EcoVadis carbon scorecard levels explained
short: The carbon scorecard rates how well you manage emissions on five levels: Insufficient, Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced and Leader. The level is based on your carbon governance, actions and reporting. Companies with 25 or fewer employees cannot get one.
audience: Indian MSME suppliers whose buyer asks for an EcoVadis carbon scorecard

sections.h: A separate scorecard from your sustainability score
p: Your EcoVadis sustainability scorecard gives a 0 to 100 score across four themes. The carbon scorecard sits beside it and grades only carbon management, with strengths and improvement areas listed. A buyer counting its Scope 3 emissions reads it to judge how far along you are in managing carbon.
You can get it through the full sustainability plans, or through a Carbon Rating plan that covers carbon questions only and is offered when a buyer invites you.

EcoVadis's 2026 analysis of about 56,000 companies rated on carbon shows the climb gets harder at each step. On reassessment, 43% of Insufficient companies moved up to Beginner and 32% of Beginners moved to Intermediate, but only 16% of Intermediate companies reached Advanced.

ul: Beginner: 81% of companies at this level have taken first actions on Scope 1 and 2, but only 9% have a target or plan.
Intermediate: 68% have a carbon target or plan. Having a target or plan is the biggest difference these figures show.

Advanced and above: companies that broke through often tied management pay to emission cuts, worked with their own suppliers on reductions, collected Scope 3 data from suppliers, adopted a dated transition plan and set a budget for it.

sections.h: A realistic path for a 60-person unit
ol: Measure: a full year of Scope 1 and 2 from electricity bills and fuel invoices, for every site, with the documents.
Act: record actions with dates and numbers, such as a solar rooftop, a boiler fuel switch or an LED retrofit with before and after units.
Commit: write a dated reduction target with a base year, signed by the owner.
Repeat: measure again next year and show the change. Your level is updated when you are reassessed.

senseible: Senseible covers the measure step: it turns your electricity bills and fuel invoices into Scope 1 and 2 figures by site and period, each tied to its document, so you can share a traceable figure with your buyer. The carbon level itself is set by EcoVadis.
